paragraphs.text: Welcome back to another episode of Tis the Podcast. The podcast that is determined to keep the Christmas spirit alive 365 days a year. This is getting harder as our temperatures are crossing well over the 100 degree mark. I'm Thom. I'm Julia. And I'm Anthony.
Tonight we're covering the VeggieTales Christmas special, and I'm so excited.
I'm out. I'm hosting. We're doing whatever I want.

I believe I have control of the Zoom. crap y'all pumpkin spice comes back next week holy crap next week it's already in the source everywhere at duncan and then the at starbucks the week after this year starbucks has a peanuts collaboration so they're gonna sell peanuts mugs and you know the thermoses and things like that. Marty said between August 1st and August 31st, right? It's the 31st month?
No, it's the 30th. It is? No, it's the 31st.
We lose like 36 minutes of light?

Freaking A. Fine by the way. I mean, I love it, but I had no idea it was that rapid. I don't need it. but isn't that going to feel like fall? It is going to feel like fall. I can't wait, y'all. I can't wait. Thank you, brother.
What'd you say? Can't wait for fall, y'all. I'm super excited for fall, y'all.
Our heat index was over 110 today. It was just miserable. It feels like a hair dryer blowing on you.
It has been like that here recently, too.
And you've got all the humidity. Speaking of that, the guy who invented the heat index scale died recently of a heat-related illness.
Hopefully he's not somewhere where he has to keep track of the heat.
Boy, that'd be awful.
He was 77, but he said he felt 92.
Oh, stop it. Did he really die, or was that whole thing…
I don't know who it was.
Oh my gosh, that was good.
So this Saturday, I'm going to Universal's Passholder Night, which I'm excited about.
I hope that's at night.

Well, it's basically customer appreciation for annual passholders. You get to stay after the park closes, and they do free food and drinks and rare character meet-and-greets, like the Ghostbusters and Doc Brown and all the classic Universal people, and you get all the rides after dark. So I'm excited.
I'm so excited for you. That's going to be incredible.
Yes, I'm excited.
I hope it'll cool off a little for you.
Oh yeah, right. I hope so too. Otherwise, I'm going to just do the water rides first.
Oh, there you go. That's a good one. You dry as the temperatures get cooler. It's pretty smart.
I mean, those rides soak you anyway.
Yeah. Do you get Islands of Adventure and Universal?
Actually, that's a good question. I'm not sure.
Oh. What are the water rides at Universal?
I don't think they have them at Universal.

Oh, that's Islands. Islands has the Dudley Do-Right Ripsaw Falls, which gets you soaked, and Jurassic Park, which is closed anyway till November, because they've been updating it. It's been closed since like March.
Boy, that one gets you stupid soaked.
Not compared to Popeye's. Popeye's gets you the most.
Are you serious?
Have you ever been on Popeye's? It's a river rapids thing. You're in the tube, but it's literally like you jumped into a pool fully clothed. You are drenched.
Oh my gosh.
And the Universal water rides are cruel anyway, because they have tons of areas where people can squirt water and shoot you with water and everything like that, too.
Yeah, that is cruel. Is that why you get so soaked?
No. Besides the rapids themselves, you're going under things, passing through waterfalls and things like that. They try to get you soaked.
Oh man. But it's nice on a nice hot day.
Oh, heck yeah. Until… you know they're bad when they've got those human dryers when you get off the ride.
Well, they don't work well anyway.
Oh, they don't. They feel good for like two minutes, but you're still soaked through, man.
I like your strategy. Let us know if it's also Islands of Adventure, because I would just love to hang out more in an emptier park, in all the Harry Potter parts.

So, Harry Potter. Y'all, we talked about this briefly off-mic, but Gilderoy Lockhart's already been cast for season two. So exciting. Nicholas Hoult is playing him, most recently seen in Superman as Lex Luthor.
I love that casting.
He'll be great. Like Julia said, I can already hear it.
Yep. And I love that they're already full steam ahead on season two, and season one hasn't premiered yet.
Christmas Eve, right? Christmas Day?
Season one, Christmas Day. Nothing like spending Christmas with the Dursleys, because the Dursleys are obviously episode one.
I'm going to get HBO Max again.
Or just my hog in.
I can't wait.
That's something I'm willing to support financially, though. Ted Lasso has been back too, which has been wonderful.
Has it been really good? I still haven't watched the original.
It has been really good. I mean, tomorrow is only episode two, but the first episode is really good.
Okay, good. It starts good. That's great.
Yeah. What movies have you seen lately?
I've seen a lot, probably, since we last talked. It's been a few weeks.
It's been a while.
I did see Pinocchio: Unstrung.
And how was it?
Of all those Twisted Childhood movies, that one was probably the best one.
Are they getting incrementally better?
That one actually felt like a movie, and they used an actual animatronic, which is cool. Previously in the series…
There's Steamboat, right?
No, he's not in there. There are two Winnie-the-Pooh ones, a Peter Pan one, and a Bambi one.
Have they gotten progressively better?
Yeah, except for Bambi, maybe. But they have a Sleeping Beauty one in the works, a Snow White one in the works, and a Mary Poppins one in the works.
They can't do that to her.
Well, actually, the rumor is she's going to be the big villain in the big Avengers-type team-up movie. Okay, so I'm excited. I saw Spider-Man.
Yep. What did you think?
Loved it. That was the best Marvel movie ever, and maybe my favorite Spider-Man movie.
Oh my gosh. Okay.
Very New York. Jon Bernthal was great as the Punisher. It was great.
Okay. My kids have seen it.
Did they like it?
Not Jude. Oh yeah, they all loved it. I mean, Gabe's just kind of whatever. He just goes and sees stuff with his girlfriend, but now we're like, that was a really good movie.
Is Gabe like Andy on The Office, when Andy tries to be a critic? "That movie is good."
Pretty much. Yeah, he never says a movie's bad. He's like, "It was good."
I saw that Olivia Wilde movie, I Want Your Sex. That one was fun.
Of course you did.
And that Amazon movie, The Devil's Mouth, which is a shark creature feature. It was okay.
Okay.

I saw Soulm8te, which was straight to streaming, but it's a Blumhouse movie. It's like a spinoff of M3GAN, but for adults, with a sex doll. It was like M3GAN meets Obsession, almost. But because M3GAN 2.0 did so badly, they sent it straight to streaming. But it was all right.
Did you say "because M3GAN tooted so bad"?
M3GAN 2.0 did so bad.
I thought you said "M3GAN tooted so bad."
Julia thought the same thing.
I did. I thought that was a cute way to say that it bombed. It really tooted so bad. That was precious. I was going to be like, I'm using that.
I saw One Night Only, which is really cute.
Loved that one, actually. One Night Only.
Yeah, that's like… what's that?
Two love-starved strangers crash into each other on the one night of the year when single people are allowed to have sex, in a dystopian America. It's a romantic comedy.
Oh, I love Callum Turner, whatever his name is.
Yeah. And I love Monica Barbaro. But it's really cute.
What was the one, Soulmate?
Soulm8te, with an eight instead of an A.
What? Oh, my brain was like, soulmate. Oh, I see. All one word. I was going to look it up. So I'm assuming this Lydia character is the sex doll? The blonde?
Yeah, yeah.
Just curious. Dungeon Crawler Carl future castings for Samantha.
Oh, that was going to be my next question. How far into it are you?
I'm in The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.
Oh, so that's the Christmas one?
Yeah, I've got two books left.
I loved the Christmas parts. So, Thom, real quick, I'm going to talk a spoiler, so if you want to take out your earphones…
Oh. Earmuffs.
How sad was it when Miriam Dom died? Like, Pony's reaction. Did that get you?
Yes, that totally got me. There have been a few moments that got me in this one. This one's been very heartfelt.
Yeah. I love Pony, though.
I know. I love Pony too. And I love that he's somehow still one of the number one crawlers, and he's just this badass.
Yep. Yeah, I love him too.
I assume we'll get more Pony as we go along, because he's not been in this one much.
Well, they were supposed to go to… where were they supposed to be? The Bahamas. But she picked a Cuba accident.
Yes, exactly. So he's just been chatting with them a few times.
Yeah. I love Donut and Mongo, though.
I do too. Mongo's the best.
And Samantha's so fun. I love Samantha. What a funny, wonderful way they have established a relationship with her as a part of the group.
Yeah. And Carl's frustration with her, but softness toward her, and encouraging her that she's part of the team. I just freaking love it so much. It's so good.
Yeah, it is so clever, that whole thing. And I just love the little found family: Donut, Carl, Mongo, Samantha, Mordecai. It's just right up my alley.
So you got to everything with B?
Yeah, I mean, that was the beginning, when they brought her on the show.
Yeah, yeah, that's what I mean. Donut finally got a chance to tell her off.
Yep.
This doesn't work, because I have to edit the podcast.
Oh, you can leave all this in. Everything can be left in after this. You'll hear it.
Oh, I don't think I'm going to start talking Dungeon Crawler Carl. I'll just skip.
Do we want to do a Dungeon Crawler Carl Christmas episode?
That would be fun. But you've got to read this book first.
I read the first one.
Well, this one's actually the fourth or fifth one.
Sixth, right? I can skip ahead. It doesn't matter. I've got two left. You will be confused if you go from one to five. Yeah, don't do that.
Well, I'm in the middle of the wandering and I'm not leaving it. So I guess y'all can do it without me.
We can do it at any time of the year. You should let us know when you get to this one.

All right. What else have you seen? that's pretty much i mean i've been doing all my horror movie watches for the bracket scare-a-thon i start july 5th and then just go to halloween that's why i call halloween spooky season watching okay how is the bracket going and cheer-a-thon how is the bracket going. Good ish. We're recording again this Sunday. Okay. But I mean, yeah, it's some of it is not pointing fingers at any show who got to pick their movies, but there have been some slogs.
Next year, though, Kendall had a good idea that I agree with: instead of movies, it's going to be a bracket for the best horror villain.
Oh, that could be really good.
And then you just argue them down.
Well, that'd be a six-hour episode.
Because a good villain could be in a crappy movie. The movies have nothing to do with it if the villain is good. So yeah, it'll be a good one.
Yeah, that'd be fun. I'll listen to that.
Yeah. Good things.
Okay, good things. I'm so excited for spooky season, though. I love going out and seeing all the fall stuff. I went to Spirit Halloween for the first time this season.
I saw that. It was fun.
They had cool animatronics. I'm not a Five Nights at Freddy's fan, but the animatronic they have of Freddy Fazbear… I mean, it's like $450, but that thing looks high-quality.
They have a lot of cool ones. Jason, Michael, Ghostface. I just don't have room for all of them.
I already have one. You need a yard.
No, you know what? They're not made for the yard. They stay in the boxes. A lot of those are for indoor use only.
Really?
Because, yeah, I don't know why. They can't get wet or whatever. But I mean, it'll last as long, I would assume, if you put them outside.
Yeah. I need a bigger house.
So do you. Besides, though, I'm super excited for what we're talking about tonight.

Well, I have something to say. I went to Walgreens to get a prescription, and I walked in and immediately smelled the cinnamon pinecone broom things, and it felt like it dropped 10 degrees. It was marvelous.

I saw this amazing reel today on Instagram. You remember the very original Spider-Man, with Willem Dafoe's Green Goblin, how the Goblin's mask would talk to him in the evil voice? The caption on the reel was "when you want to decorate in October but haven't yet," and it's just this scary-looking pumpkin looking out of the closet, and it's like, "You know you want to do it," talking with the little Dafoe audio, while the guy's trying to ignore it. It was very funny.
I love that.
I do love that.
I love what we're talking about tonight.
Me too.
Veggie Tales. Julia and I grew up with this show.

And we love it. Anthony kind of lacks a soul. So I think he is why he hates it. That's the only thing that makes sense. But I'm hoping that when we talk Veggie Tales, we can help his heart to grow two sizes larger.
I do. The Grinch Screw 3. wait, before we actually talk about tonight, we do have some Christmas. What did you guys think of the Ebenezer trailer?
With Johnny Depp? The tone is weird.
I'm afraid. My fear is we're going to hit a Charlie and the Chocolate Factory situation.
That's my fear too, because all he knows how to play is a weird dude with a weird, not-quite-British accent.

The ghosts look awesome. The Ghost of Christmas Past looks terrifying. I mean, he looks great, the set looks great, the ghosts look great. But the cast… they have Ian McKellen and Daisy Ridley and Rupert Grint. Ron Weasley is playing Bob Cratchit. But yeah, the tone… I don't view Scrooge as a funny dude.
I don't either.
No. And then, what did you all think of the Violent Night 2 trailer? Because I watched that one, with Kristen Bell.
I have not watched that one yet. I need to watch that one.

Oh, well, the trailer gives the premise of this movie away. Santa himself has lost his magic. He's on the naughty list, because he's like, "I don't know, maybe I killed too many people," referencing the first one. But he's stuck in a shopping mall without his powers, as a mall Santa.
Oh no.
And the mall basically gets a Die Hard-type situation, and he has to take down all the terrorists attacking the mall.
Oh my gosh. It's set in a mall? Oh, that looks beautiful.
Oh geez. Oh, yes. I love it.
Oh, absolutely. I am here for it. I'm going to watch it as soon as we're done today.

Also, Ghosts isn't coming back till midseason this year, but they are coming back, and they are doing two episodes: an hour-long Halloween special and an hour-long Christmas special, even though they're not coming back until January. And the hour-long Christmas special this year, they said, is going to be their version of Die Hard. So that should be…
Oh jeez. Okay. We've got good stuff to look forward to. I'm excited.

Also, one other Christmas-related thing: Steven Beech, our good friend Disco54, messaged me saying he had a bone to pick with us, because we had him on that time and then lost the recording, obviously. But he said he gave us a whole list of British specials to cover, and we said we would, and we haven't done one of them. And I was like, in our defense, we lost the list, because we lost the recording.
And did he give us the list?
Yeah, he did. So we've got it.
Of course he did. Of course he did.
So I love it. Disco, I can't promise that stuff will be done this year, because we're about to enter spooky season, and then all the new stuff comes out. But definitely starting in January, for sure.
Okay. Yeah, yeah. Let's go.
So what are we covering tonight? You tell us, Thom.
I tried, and you didn't like my idea. I guess we'll talk The Office again, for some reason, even though we've already done this. Why would we do a second episode on The Office, Anthony?

Well, because Peacock has released all the Superfan extended episodes of the show, and they were just made available to purchase on Vudu as well. So now, when Peacock eventually takes them away, I have them on my Vudu.
And they're taking it away?

Well, no, but you know streamers. Eventually. So I am super excited to cover The Office extended Christmas episodes. When we covered these way back when, we covered them all in one go, but we're splitting them over a few weeks. We can't do that with the extended editions, and that episode got long anyway.
I mean, that's still one of my favorite episodes. But yes, this will give us time to breathe and talk about them in more detail.
Yes. So I'm super excited. All right, we don't need to do the cast. We've talked about this cast a lot. I guess we just jump in, right? The first one: "Office Christmas Party," right?
Wait, what was it called?
It's called "Christmas Party."

"Christmas Party." So, I'm trying to figure out how we should do this. And full disclosure, I texted this to Anthony earlier: it's been a while since I've watched these. I wish they would show me the extended parts and flag them in such a way that I know it's extra content, because it's been so long since I've seen them. And Anthony's like, "That's what I'm here for." I'm like, totally fair. You do know these up, down, and sideways.
So we need to set the stage, first of all, with what this is. This is season two, episode 10, "Christmas Party." They added seven minutes, which got a little weird.

As a reminder, we are here for an office Christmas party. Michael organizes a big Secret Santa swap. The big thing is, he bought Ryan an iPod, and he gets a handmade gift from Phyllis. And he decides, instead of people getting the gifts that were bought for them, he wants to do a… they call it Yankee swap. We call it Dirty Santa.

We went through this on the last episode, and I still have never heard "Nasty Santa" in real life. White Elephant I've heard. But "Nasty Christmas," I've never heard that anywhere but The Office. Have you?
No. Okay. We don't talk about Yankees where I come from.
Yankee swap I've even heard of. Not Nasty Christmas, not Nasty Santa, or Dirty Santa.

No. And he turns it into this whole thing, because he was so upset with the gift he received, because he broke his own rule, which was a $20 limit on the gift. He ruins Christmas by forcing them to play Yankee swap. And obviously everybody got specific gifts for who they got, including Jim, who got a teapot for Pam and filled it with all these inside jokes, and has a letter in there to tell her how he feels. Because Christmas is a time to tell people how you feel, even though she's engaged. She's not married yet. To quote Michael on the booze cruise: "BFD. Engaged ain't married."
What? He's so bad.
"BFD. Engaged ain't married." That's what he tells Jim on the booze cruise.
Oh my gosh. I thought you said Blue's Clues for a second there, and I was like, hold the phone, I missed that episode.
We have a longer time with Pam holding Jim's gift, too, right?

Yes. It felt more extended. So there's much more of the gift swapping and seeing what people got each other. Michael has a great talking head where he explains who each employee is at Christmastime. He compares Dwight to the monster who puts a star on top of the tree, and Rudolph. He also claims that Dwight looks like Spock, which is referencing the ears he's wearing, right? And that was also extra. And that annoys Dwight, because he has specific Vulcan ears that are different.

I did enjoy that. Okay, I'm confused. There was a bit where the party planning committee is decorating the tree, and Dwight is asking who's coming to the party, and Phyllis mentions she has a new boyfriend, Bob Vance, who's coming. And Dwight remarks to Pam that she must feel pretty bad, because even Phyllis has someone coming to the party, and she doesn't, because at this point Roy was not coming to the party. The Bob Vance stuff, was that part extra?
Well, no. He was in the original, with "Bob Vance, Vance Refrigeration," but that stuff was extra.

He was just brought in and introduced in the original, right, Anthony? Got it. Where he just says everybody Bob Vance, Vance Refrigeration, and he shakes their hands. So Kelly gets mad at Oscar for not liking her gift, which is the shower radio, and Oscar has a talking head with the camera where he tells the camera that Kelly got the same gift last year. Last year.
Well, Oscar also has a thing with why he gave Creed the gift, right?
Where he got him the... Shamrock? Or four-leaf clover, not shamrock.
Oh, and there's this whole bit where Kevin karaokes "Christmas in Hollis." In the original, "Christmas in Hollis" is just played. Kevin wasn't karaoke-ing it.
Yeah. Yep. I liked this. I liked it a lot more.
Yep. He sings an entire verse.
Yes. I don't know why they cut that.

Dwight explains to the camera that he has to remain sober because he's an officer of the law and he can't get drunk. There was also another scene where, when they're going for drinks at the end, Roy agrees and suggests Chili's, and Pam says, "Can't. Lifetime ban." Which I appreciate. That callback.
And then Michael has some other talking heads, talking about things like how he loves it when people envy the gift you gave someone else.
He's such a jerk, man.

Well, when Phyllis storms out, it's slightly different in this version, because Meredith takes the oven mitt from Oscar, and Michael is like, "Like anybody would want an oven mitt." And then Phyllis storms out. But I just love his obliviousness: "I wonder what makes her so angry."
Right. Immediately. She gets mad, and he's like, "What's she so…" So oblivious.

That part made me laugh too. There's not even a breath in between. Which reminds me: I just bought this on Vudu, so I've been watching from the beginning, and I got to the episode last night where Andy punches a hole in the wall, and Dwight's working at Staples, and Michael goes to bring him back and everything like that. But when Michael's hiding from Andy behind his office door, he's talking about, "How can anyone have so little self-awareness?" It just reminded me of this.

So, back in the day, when this episode first aired, we talked about this last time: this episode is often credited with saving the show, because the video iPod was a big thing at the time, and I guess they released this one for free or whatever on iTunes.
Yeah. Oh, that's funny.
And all the photos Michael takes on his digital camera, Steve Carell was actually taking, and they posted them on the NBC website after this episode.
Including Meredith?

Well, I don't know about that one. And I know it's not new content, it was in the original, but it never fails… Steve Carell's a great actor, but it's just his face. He turns around and starts to avert it, and then he feels bad, grabs the camera, clicks it, and walks away. So I loved the original, but the extra stuff makes it so much funnier. It gives things time to breathe.
Yeah. And for some reason, the extended version also feels a little more Christmassy than the non-extended version.
Yeah. Maybe it's because… I don't know. We always talk about how we love how the Brits do those extended Christmas episodes, and we don't so much over here, which I actually appreciate.
Speaking of the Brits, the woman who played Dawn on the British Office, the Pam equivalent… she was in Wonder Woman, I forget her name… she was just diagnosed with terminal cancer.
Oh gosh.
Sad. But yeah, this one was great. I just love this world and these characters. It makes me wish I worked in an office.
It's so funny, because you watch the show and you wish you went to an office like this, but they all hate their lives.

Something I like about all the Christmas episodes of The Office is how they end up, for the most part, rallying at the end, and they do in this one too. Michael never apologized to Phyllis, but he makes everyone feel better by going out and buying a bunch of booze.
I love that. I love that scene. "You're the expert here. Will this get 20 people drunk?" 13 bottles. "Yeah, that should do it. Box it up."
Also, I love when it's Steve Carell's last episode, and Michael's leaving the show, and it's a callback: Phyllis is knitting him mittens for Colorado, and he's actually grateful.
Oh, yeah. He wants her to finish them before he leaves.
He had growth.
Better than a growth.
I was thinking the same thing but wasn't going to say it.
I know Thom loves the next one, because of Michael and his Christmas card.

I do. I do. But before we get into that, I learned something from Jenna Fischer about Benihana. I learned about their history. Like any good story, they're known for saying, the history of Benihana begins with the descendant of a samurai warrior in a small Tokyo coffee shop. Do we want to know about the history of Benihana, or do we just want to jump into something else?
Sure.

This is from Jenna. A couple in Tokyo started a coffee shop, and in order to set themselves apart and get more business, the husband would bike 20 miles to get real sugar to serve with the coffee, and that helped it become a huge success. They named their coffee shop Benihana. So if we jump ahead, their son Rocky comes to the United States, and he wants to open a restaurant. He goes to night school to learn about restaurant management. During the day, he sold ice cream in Harlem, New York, and to set it apart, he put the little Japanese cocktail umbrella in it. And people loved that little touch. And so he earned $10,000, which he used to open his first Benihana restaurant, which he named after his parents' coffee shop in Tokyo.
Oh my gosh.
So that was fun.
I have to ask the requisite: are you bullcrapping us right now?

I also learned from her that this was, in fact, the real Benihana. They hired all of the chefs and all of the wait staff from the Encino Benihana to be in this episode. The waitresses were actual servers, and they brought in 78 actors to look like they were eating in the background, and they rented the restaurant out and shut it down for the entire 12 hours they needed to record. Angela Kinsey said it reminded her of how big a budget they had by this point, because when they did Chili's, they found an out-of-business, boarded-up Chili's that they just sort of took over.
Things had changed a little bit.
Yeah, so they grew a little bit. But yeah, at the beginning of this one, Michael is dating Carol, who was his realtor when he bought his condo.
And his real-life wife.
And his real-life wife. Which, I'm sorry, when you know that, and you watch this and see the way she reacts to his humor, I feel like we're getting a little insight into the Carell home.
I really do. Marty said it's so funny that they're actually married in real life, because she seems so put out with him most of the time.

She does. But she ends up breaking up with him, because Michael has the really smart idea that he should take her vacation photo from when she and her husband and kids went to Colorado and Photoshop himself in place of her husband, and that's his Christmas card that he's going to send out to everybody.
His "too far" is just so good.

One of the extended scenes of this is where Ryan says Michael has a history of Photoshopping himself into pictures. For example: "I never went to Egypt with him," and it's Michael on a camel with Ryan.
Even though Steve Carell and his wife have kids, these are not their kids. They had his wife pose with a random tall guy and a couple of kids, and then literally Photoshopped
Steve Carell's face on top of it.
Was that to get around having his kids?
No, I don't know. I think it was to show how bad a Photoshop it was, rather than using a real picture. I think that had a lot to do with it.
Because their real kids were on the show before, as her kids, in the Michael's birthday episode, where they're at the ice skating rink. Those are his real kids.
Oh my gosh. I love it.

This is also where he tried to surprise her with a vacation to Sandals over the holidays, when she's a mom. And he's so put out by the breakup that he hooks up with a random Benihana waitress, brings a different one back to the office, and then confuses which one he brought back with the one Andy brought back, and marks one with a marker, because all waitresses look the same.

And then, of course, he and Jim have the heart-to-heart, where Jim is like, it's a rebound, and at the end of the day, you're left thinking about the woman you really care about. And you see Michael calling somebody else to invite them to Sandals, and whoever it is agrees, and he's super happy. And who does it end up being?
Jan.
Jan, that's right.
Well, there are definitely deleted and extended scenes put back into this episode, including Ryan talking about the Photoshop, and the dumpster scene.
The dumpster scene.

So Kelly claims she threw out the gift she got Ryan, and then she's in the dumpster looking for it, and he's cold, and she starts crying, and he climbs in, and they start having sex in the dumpster. And you hear them: "Here's your Christmas gift." "You like your present?"
I can't stand Ryan anyway, so that was like, ugh. And it's just amazing to me that B.J. Novak writes his character to be so freaking hated. There is nothing redemptive about him in the entire show.
Well, Jim has this line when he comes back from Stamford: "I liked you better as a temp." And Ryan was like, "Me too." And I was like, yeah, I think the audience did too.
Oh, that's funny.
Another extended scene is Angela stringing popcorn and expressing her outrage on behalf of baby Jesus: you can't cancel Christmas because you got dumped.
What was the Christmas? It wasn't supposed to be Benihana Christmas. What was it supposed to be? What?
Not back for Christmas.
Yeah, so that's the other storyline, the dueling parties. We're not there yet.
